title: Purity criterion using a pure etale chart and the relative assassin
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $F$ a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and $s\in S$. Let $e:(S^{\prime},s^{\prime})\to(S,s)$ be an elementary etale neighbourhood [def-sfb-scheme-relative-purity]. Let $g:X^{\prime}\to X$ and $p:X^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ satisfy $fg=ep$. Assume: $F$ is flat over $S$ at every point of $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over, def-pc-scheme-fibre]; $p$ is of finite type; $g^*F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is pure along $X^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}}$ [def-sfb-scheme-relative-purity]; $g$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]; and $g(X^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}})$ contains $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(F_s)$ [def-trf-relative-assassin]. Put $Y=X\times_SS^{\prime}$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $F_Y=\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$, and $h=(g,p):X^{\prime}\to Y$. Then $F$ is pure along $X_s$ if and only if $h(X^{\prime})$ contains every point of $\operatorname{Ass}_{Y/S^{\prime}}(F_Y)$ lying over a generalization of $s^{\prime}$. A generalization $t$ of $s^{\prime}$ means $s^{\prime}\in\overline{\{t\}}$.

proof.text: Write $q:Y\to S^{\prime}$ and $G=g^*F$. Base change preserves finite type, so $q$ is finite type. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence and finite type, so $F_Y$ and $G$ have these properties. The pullback-composition isomorphism gives $h^*F_Y\cong G$, since $\operatorname{pr}_Xh=g$. The projection $Y\to X$ is etale by base change of $e$; cancellation with its etale composite $g$ makes $h$ etale. Thus $W=h(X^{\prime})$ is open in $Y$. The residue-field isomorphism $\kappa(s)\cong\kappa(s^{\prime})$ identifies $Y_{s^{\prime}}$ with $X_s$ and their sheaves. Under this identification $h$ on $X^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}}$ is $g$, so the corrected coverage hypothesis implies $\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_{s^{\prime}}}((F_Y)_{s^{\prime}})\subset W$.

source.place: Tag 05L4 (lemma-criterion), first paragraph; fibre coverage corrected as documented in report.md.

proof.text: The sheaf $F_Y$ is flat over $S^{\prime}$ at every $y\in Y_{s^{\prime}}$: its image $x$ is in $X_s$, so $F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ by hypothesis; the pullback-stalk formula identifies $(F_Y)_y$ with $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}F_x$, and the pointwise relative-flat-extension lemma makes this flat over $\mathcal O_{S^{\prime},s^{\prime}}$. This uses flatness only on the specified fibre.

source.place: Tag 05L4 (lemma-criterion), base change in the first paragraph; morphisms.tex lemma-base-change-module-flat.

proof.text: Purity of $F$ along $X_s$ implies purity of $F_Y$ along $Y_{s^{\prime}}$ directly from the definition. Indeed, for any elementary etale neighbourhood $(T,t)\to(S^{\prime},s^{\prime})$, its composite with $e$ is etale by composition and induces the composite of two residue-field isomorphisms, hence is elementary over $(S,s)$. The iterated fibre product is $X_T$ and its sheaf is the same tensor pullback of $F$, by pullback composition. An impurity for $F_Y$ on this neighbourhood would therefore be an impurity for $F$. Conversely, if $F_Y$ is pure along $Y_{s^{\prime}}$, flat-point descent proves purity of $F$ along $X_s$, since the etale map $e$ is flat at $s^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 05L4 (lemma-criterion), first paragraph; elementary-neighbourhood case of purity ascent, and Tag 05J9 (lemma-flat-descend-pure).

proof.text: Assume $F$ is pure. By step 3, $F_Y$ is pure along $Y_{s^{\prime}}$. Let $a\in\operatorname{Ass}_{Y/S^{\prime}}(F_Y)$ lie above a generalization of $s^{\prime}$. The identity of $S^{\prime}$ is an elementary neighbourhood; the definition of purity therefore gives $z\in\overline{\{a\}}\cap Y_{s^{\prime}}$. Give $Z=\overline{\{a\}}$ its reduced induced closed-subscheme structure. Its underlying space is irreducible: if two closed subsets cover it, one contains $a$ and hence its closure. Thus $Z$ is integral. The fibre $Z_{s^{\prime}}$ is nonempty because it contains $z$. Choose a component $C$ containing $z$ by irreducible-component coverage, and its generic point $b$ by sobriety of the scheme $Z_{s^{\prime}}$. Apply the flat relative-associated specialization lemma to $q,F_Y,a,C,b$: finite type and finite type quasi-coherence hold by step 1, and flatness at $b$ holds by step 2. It gives $b\in\operatorname{Ass}_{Y/S^{\prime}}(F_Y)$, hence $b\in\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_{s^{\prime}}}((F_Y)_{s^{\prime}})$. Step 1 gives $b\in W$. Since $b\in Z$, $a$ specializes to $b$; an open containing $b$ contains $a$. Consequently $a\in W$, proving the required containment.

source.place: Tag 05L4 (lemma-criterion), second paragraph; expansion of Tag 05L3 (lemma-associated-point-specializes) using more-morphisms.tex Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes).

proof.text: Conversely assume the asserted containment in $W$. Take any elementary etale neighbourhood $v:(T,t)\to(S^{\prime},s^{\prime})$. Write $Y_T=Y\times_{S^{\prime}}T$, $X^{\prime}_T=X^{\prime}\times_{S^{\prime}}T$, and $h_T:X^{\prime}_T\to Y_T$. For any $a\in\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_T/T}((F_Y)_T)$ lying over $u\leadsto t$, relative-assassin base change implies that its image $a_0\in Y$ is in $\operatorname{Ass}_{Y/S^{\prime}}(F_Y)$. Continuity gives $v(u)\leadsto s^{\prime}$, so the containment assumption gives $a_0\in W$. The base-change image equality gives a point $b\in X^{\prime}_T$ with $h_T(b)=a$; necessarily $b$ lies over $u$. No equality of the entire inverse image with the relative assassin is needed here, only the implication from upstairs associated points to downstairs ones.

The fibre map $(h_T)_u:(X^{\prime}_T)_u\to(Y_T)_u$ is etale by base change of $h$. Both fibre schemes are finite type over $\kappa(u)$, by finite-type base change applied to $p$ and $q$; they are locally Noetherian by the finite-type-over-locally-Noetherian lemma (a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal). The pullbacks of $F_Y$ and $G$ are quasi-coherent. Pullback composition identifies the pullback of $((F_Y)_T)_u$ by $(h_T)_u$ with $(G_T)_u$. Etale associated-point invariance on these locally Noetherian fibres therefore makes $b$ a point of $\operatorname{Ass}_{X^{\prime}_T/T}(G_T)$. This checks the Noetherian hypotheses on the fibres only; neither $S^{\prime}$ nor $T$ is assumed Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 05L4 (lemma-criterion), final paragraph; fibrewise use of Tag 05FP (lemma-etale-weak-assassin-up-down), in its existing locally-Noetherian associated-point form.

proof.text: By the assumed purity of $G$ along $X^{\prime}_{s^{\prime}}$, the elementary neighbourhood $(T,t)$ and the relative associated point $b$ over $u\leadsto t$ admit a specialization $b\leadsto c$ with $c\in(X^{\prime}_T)_t$. Its image gives $a=h_T(b)\leadsto h_T(c)\in(Y_T)_t$. Thus every relative associated point above a generalization of $t$ has a specialization in this fibre. Since $(T,t)$ was arbitrary, the definition says that $F_Y$ is pure along $Y_{s^{\prime}}$. Step 3 then descends this purity to $F$ along $X_s$. This proves the reverse implication.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the source and imported coverage hypothesis g(X prime) contains Ass(X_s,F_s) is insufficient when other points of S prime lie over s. Corrected it to coverage by the distinguished fibre g(X prime_s prime). Gave the explicit two-copy field counterexample in report.md and audited the sole citer. Seven proof steps use existing nodes only; the relative-associated specialization input is the existing more general Tag 0GSI node, not a new Tag 05L3 duplicate. Every citation has a verbatim quotation in citations.json.

tool_uses.why: Step 4 uses only the associated-point conclusion at a generic point of a special-fibre component. This is exactly the more general existing input behind Tag 05L3; no node of the item unit states it.

Step 5 uses only image containment of relative associated points under arbitrary base change; the existing Tag 05DC statement gives it. This is the source criterion's own algebraic tool, not another route.
Step 2 uses the pointwise stalk flatness conclusion to retain flatness on the special fibre under base change; a global flatness lemma would have insufficient hypotheses.
Step 2 uses the actual pullback stalk tensor isomorphism to apply pointwise relative-flat extension.
Step 4 gives the closure of the relative associated point its reduced induced closed scheme structure for the existing specialization lemma.
Step 4 obtains a generic point of a component of the nonempty special fibre of that closure.
Step 4 obtains a component through a known point of the special fibre.
Step 6 verifies local Noetherianity of both fibre schemes before applying etale associated-point invariance.
Step 5 lifts a point of the inverse image of the chart image along the base-changed chart; this is an equality of point images, not a cartesian assertion about underlying sets.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NN-7213d56fc (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Stacks flat.tex 05L4 (lemma-criterion) and its proof, 05L3, every cited node and the item's 7 steps; there are no new nodes. The source is wrong. I checked the worker's counterexample myself: S=X=Spec k, S'=Spec k⊔Spec k with the fold map, X' mapped into the second copy, g=id. Hypotheses (1)-(5) hold, F is pure, but s' is not in h(X'). The fix replaces (5) by g(X'_{s'}) ⊇ Ass_{X_s}(F_s), which is exactly what the source's step 'replace S by S'' needs. Every other hypothesis and both directions are kept, and the error is reported under ## Source error. Step checks: (1) base change, cancellation and openness give W=h(X') open and the corrected hypothesis gives Ass_{Y_{s'}} ⊆ W; (2) flatness on the special fibre via the pointwise stalk lemma; (3) ascent by composing elementary neighbourhoods, descent by 05J9; (4) identity neighbourhood, reduced closure, a component and its generic point, then 0GSI with flatness only at that point, and the open W is stable under generalization; (5) only the 'only if' half of 05DC, then the base-change image node; (6) the fibres are locally Noetherian because they are of finite type over a field, and 05FP fibrewise invariance applies; (7) purity of G pushed forward by h_T. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. Batch 5: I accept lem-sfb-scheme-etale-assassin-invariance, lem-trf-flat-relative-associated-specialization (0GSI) and lem-trf-relative-assassin-base-change (05DC) as generic commutative algebra about relative assassins. Their closures contain no trace-formula, Poincaré or nt-* theorem, neither assumption gives them, and none is a step of either proof. No SGA is cited and no duplicate of 05L4 exists. MAINTAINER NOTE for HUMAN.md: the only citer, lem-sfb-flat-fp-purity-open, has a broken step 4. It uses only X_s ⊆ g(X') from 05KW, and the counterexample meets that chart data, so the step was already deriving a false conclusion. The citer needs a chart covering X_s by X'_{s'} or another argument; its step 6 stays valid.
